In [[algebra]], a '''Lie-admissible algebra''', introduced by {{harvs|txt|first=A. Adrian|last=Albert|year=1948}},  is a (possibly [[non-associative algebra|non-associative]]) [[algebra over a field|algebra]] that becomes a [[Lie algebra]] under the bracket [''a'',&thinsp;''b''] = ''ab'' − ''ba''. Examples include [[associative algebra]]s,<ref>{{harvnb|Okubo|1995|p=19}}</ref> Lie algebras, and [[Okubo algebra]]s.
